title: When Inputs Receive No Score: Evaluating Open-Web Event Admission on the Complete Stream
abstract: arXiv:2610.17814v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: A Web item can link to the correct event without contributing information worth organizing. Evaluating item-level admission therefore begins with complete inputs, including those a processing pipeline fails to score. We study how this upstream selection changes ranking comparisons and constrains operational decisions. Across six instruction-model backbones, three strategies, and 602 human-annotated evaluation items, systems score different populations with different class compositions. Comparing rankings on shared inputs separates these population differences from discrimination. Score availability also limits attainable retention: four configurations score only ten of twelve positive development items, making a 90% full-stream target unreachable by threshold adjustment. translated_title: 当输入未获得评分时：在完整数据流上评估开放网络事件准入
translated_abstract: 一条网络条目可以链接到正确的事件，却不贡献值得组织的信息。因此，条目级别的准入评估应从完整的输入开始，包括那些处理流水线无法评分的输入。我们研究了这种上游选择如何改变排序比较并约束运营决策。在六个指令模型骨干、三种策略和602个人工标注的评估条目上，各系统对具有不同类别构成的不同条目群体进行评分。在共享输入上比较排序，可以将这些群体差异与判别能力区分开来。评分的可用性还限制了可达到的保留率：四种配置仅对十二个正类开发条目中的十个进行了评分，使得仅通过阈值调整无法达到全流90%的目标。配对的精确率实验表明，这一约束同时取决于执行配置与模型选择。Qwen 对相同数量的评估条目进行评分，未……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究提出在完整数据流（包括处理流水线无法评分的输入）上评估开放网络事件条目准入，发现评分可用性会改变排序比较结果并使可实现的保留率存在上限，导致90%全流目标无法仅靠阈值调整达成。
en_tdlr: Evaluating open-web event admission on the complete input stream, this paper shows that score availability changes ranking comparisons and caps attainable retention, making a 90% full-stream target unreachable by threshold adjustment alone.
